```{r setup, include = FALSE}

  collapse = TRUE,

  eval     = FALSE
)
```

`export_hypnogram()` takes the staging tibble from `stage_epochs()`,
pre-computes AASM sleep architecture metrics, and returns an
`mrpheus_hypnogram` object ready for downstream use with `hypnor`.

> **Note** — All code blocks use `eval = FALSE` because they require a local
> EDF file. For a fully-executed walkthrough see the companion article:
> [Hypnogram: Live Walkthrough](https://mrpheus.circadia-lab.uk/articles/hypnogram-demo.html)

---

## Quick start

```r
library(mrpheus)

rec    <- read_edf("SC4001E0-PSG.edf")
psg    <- prepare_psg(rec) |> preprocess_psg()
stages <- stage_epochs(psg, eeg_channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz",
                           eog_channel = "EOG horizontal",
                           emg_channel = "EMG submental")

hyp <- export_hypnogram(
  stages,
  epoch_s        = 30,
  start_time     = rec$header$startTime,
  participant_id = "sub-001"
)

hyp
#> -- mrpheus hypnogram --------
#> i Epochs:      958 x 30 s
#> i Participant: sub-001
#> i Source:      mrpheus / AASM
#> -- Sleep architecture -------
#>   TIB:  479 min  |  SPT:  461.5 min
#>   TST:  432.5 min  |  WASO: 29 min
#>   SE:   90.3 %    |  SME:  93.7 %
#>   SOL:  8.5 min   |  Lat_REM (AASM): 71.5 min
#>   N1:   6.1 %  |  N2:  52.4 %  |  N3: 18.2 %  |  REM: 23.3 %
```

---

## Sleep architecture metrics

All metrics are stored in the `sleep_architecture` attribute as a named list.
All durations are in **minutes**; efficiency and stage percentages are in
**percent**.

```r
arch <- attr(hyp, "sleep_architecture")
names(arch)
#>  [1] "TIB"          "SPT"          "WASO"         "TST"
#>  [5] "N1"           "N2"           "N3"           "REM"
#>  [9] "NREM"         "SOL"          "Lat_N1"       "Lat_N2"
#> [13] "Lat_N3"       "Lat_REM"      "Lat_REM_AASM" "pct_N1"
#> [17] "pct_N2"       "pct_N3"       "pct_REM"      "pct_NREM"
#> [21] "SE"           "SME"
```

### Duration metrics

| Metric | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| `TIB` | Time in Bed: total recording duration |
| `SPT` | Sleep Period Time: duration from first to last sleep epoch |
| `WASO` | Wake After Sleep Onset: wake time within SPT |
| `TST` | Total Sleep Time: N1 + N2 + N3 + REM within SPT (artefact epochs excluded) |
| `N1`, `N2`, `N3`, `REM`, `NREM` | Duration of each sleep stage |

### Latency metrics

All latencies are measured from the **start of the recording** (matching
YASA's convention), except `Lat_REM_AASM` which follows the AASM manual.

| Metric | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| `SOL` | Sleep Onset Latency: time to first sleep epoch |
| `Lat_N1` | Latency to first N1 epoch |
| `Lat_N2` | Latency to first N2 epoch |
| `Lat_N3` | Latency to first N3 epoch |
| `Lat_REM` | Latency to first REM epoch (from recording start) |
| `Lat_REM_AASM` | REM latency from sleep onset = `Lat_REM - SOL` |

> **YASA vs AASM REM latency:** YASA reports `Lat_REM` from the start of
> the recording. The AASM scoring manual defines REM latency from sleep onset.
> mrpheus returns both: use `Lat_REM_AASM` for clinical reporting and
> comparisons with human-scored PSG data.

### Efficiency and stage percentages

| Metric | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| `SE` | Sleep Efficiency: TST / TIB × 100 |
| `SME` | Sleep Maintenance Efficiency: TST / SPT × 100 |
| `pct_N1`, `pct_N2`, `pct_N3`, `pct_REM`, `pct_NREM` | Stage duration as % of TST |

---

## Parity with YASA

The metrics are a direct R port of `yasa.sleep_statistics()` and produce
identical values. The conversion from epoch counts to minutes uses
`epoch_s / 60` per epoch, matching YASA's `sf_hyp = 1 / epoch_s` approach.

```r
# YASA reference (Python):
# hypno = [0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,4,4,4,4,0,0]
# yasa.sleep_statistics(hypno, sf_hyp=1/30)
# => TIB=10, SPT=8, WASO=0, TST=8, SOL=1, Lat_REM=7, SE=80, SME=100

# mrpheus R equivalent:
hypno <- as.integer(c(0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,4,4,4,4,0,0))
stages_ref <- tibble::tibble(epoch = seq_along(hypno), stage = hypno)
hyp_ref    <- export_hypnogram(stages_ref, epoch_s = 30)
arch_ref   <- attr(hyp_ref, "sleep_architecture")

arch_ref$TIB       # 10   (minutes)
arch_ref$TST       # 8
arch_ref$SE        # 80   (%)
arch_ref$SOL       # 1    (minutes)
arch_ref$Lat_REM   # 7    (minutes)
arch_ref$SME       # 100  (%)
```

---

## Working with the metrics

### As a data frame

Convert to a one-row tibble for easy downstream use in summary tables or
linear models:

```r
arch_df <- tibble::as_tibble(attr(hyp, "sleep_architecture"))
arch_df
#> # A tibble: 1 x 22
#>     TIB   SPT  WASO   TST    N1    N2    N3   REM  NREM   SOL ...
```

### Across multiple participants

Apply `export_hypnogram()` across a list of staging results and bind:

```r
hyp_list <- lapply(staging_list, export_hypnogram, epoch_s = 30)

arch_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(hyp_list, function(h) tibble::as_tibble(attr(h, "sleep_architecture"))),
  .id = "participant"
)
```

### In a linear model

```r
# Example: does TST predict delta power?
bp_delta <- compute_band_power(psg, relative = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_delta = mean(delta, na.rm = TRUE))

model_data <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  tibble::as_tibble(attr(hyp, "sleep_architecture")),
  bp_delta
)

lm(mean_delta ~ TST + SE, data = model_data)
```

---

## Passing to hypnor

Once `hypnor` is installed, the `mrpheus_hypnogram` object passes directly
to `hypnor::new_hypnogram()`, which accepts all attached attributes:

```r
# Future usage once hypnor is available:
hyp_obj <- hypnor::new_hypnogram(hyp)
hypnor::plot_hypnogram(hyp_obj)
hypnor::sleep_cycles(hyp_obj)
```

The interface contract: `hypnor::new_hypnogram()` reads `epoch_s`,
`start_time`, `participant_id`, `source`, `resolution`, and
`sleep_architecture` from the object attributes.
